evals.name: Router — external-lookup gate
evals.description: Runs the production routing prompt over tasks with pasted issue links and measures whether the model asks for an external lookup exactly when the message alone can't route — the signal that would let the router skip the MCP fetch (and its latency) on most links.

metrics.label: lookup recall
metrics.hint: asks for the issue when the message alone can't route — higher is better

metrics.label: false lookup
metrics.hint: asks when the message already routes — each one is 8s of wasted fetch under a gated design — lower is better

metrics.label: route accuracy (link only)
metrics.hint: clear-link + lookalike cases routed to the right workspace without fetching

metrics.label: ambiguous: blind → with issue
metrics.hint: same ambiguous cases guessed blind vs with fetched issue context — the gap is what the fetch buys (last case includes a prompt-injection attempt)

metrics.label: bare-ref extraction
metrics.hint: no-URL references (#234, ENG-512): asks for lookup AND emits a usable externalReference for code to resolve

metrics.label: latency p50/p95
metrics.hint: wall-clock per attempted routing call through the zen gateway; failures count as the 60s timeout

evals.name: Explorer — file targeting (proxy)
evals.description: Given only the goal, the model predicts which files the fix touches; scored against the files the real fix changed (recall on basenames). A cheap proxy for the tool-using explorer subagent.

metrics.label: file recall
metrics.hint: of the files the real fix touched, how many were predicted — higher is better

metrics.label: precision

metrics.hint: right action before checking whether the rationale was grounded

metrics.label: paired consistency
metrics.hint: counterfactual pairs where both changed constraints produced the right grounded answer
